artworks.title: The Rape of Proserpina
artworks.description: Bernini's Borghese marble — Pluto seizing Proserpina for the underworld, the Hymn's abduction carved into yielding flesh.

artworks.title: The Return of Persephone
artworks.description: Leighton's Leeds canvas — Hermes leading Persephone up to Demeter's arms, the annual reunion that brings spring back.

artworks.title: Proserpine
artworks.description: Rossetti's Tate Proserpine holds the bitten pomegranate — the Hymn's binding fruit that splits the year between worlds.

artworks.title: Demeter Mourning for Persephone
artworks.description: De Morgan's winter goddess among withered stalks — the mother's grief that barrened the earth until the Kore returned.

artworks.title: The Demeter of Knidos
artworks.description: Seated marble from Knidos — the sorrowful mother of the mysteries, grief read into the grain-goddess' face.

popCulture.title: Homeric Hymn to Demeter
popCulture.description: The Hymn still carries Demeter's search and Persephone's pomegranate — Eleusis, the seasons, and the mother's bargain with Hades.

popCulture.title: Persephone
popCulture.description: The Kore's abduction and return remain the agricultural year personified — winter below, spring above.
